items.title: Negri Sembilan police say they are not taking sides
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police in Negri Sembilan are closely monitoring developments concerning the state's royal institution and taking necessary measures to maintain public order, without taking sides. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police took note of the Attorney-General's Chambers' statement on the April 19, 2026 proclamation and developments in the related legal process. In a statement, he said police respected the constitutional, legal and institutional processes.

items.title: Man falls from third floor of Ipoh hospital building, in critical condition
items.summary: Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police received a report about the incident at about 2.30pm, Kosmo! Online reported. He said preliminary investigations found that a hospital security guard had noticed a man behaving suspiciously in an emergency staircase.

items.title: Woman worker dies after being trapped in lifter machine in Telok Panglima Garang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A woman worker died after she was believed to have been trapped in a lifter machine at a premises in Telok Panglima Garang in Kuala Langat yesterday. Online, Kuala Langat district police chief Superintendent Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said police received a report about the incident from a local man at about 11am. Members of the public with information are urged to contact the nearest police station or the Kuala Langat district police headquarters operations room at 03-3187 2222 to assist investigations.

items.title: Narrow escape for couple after lorry plunges into ravine at Hulu Terengganu landslide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A husband and wife escaped injury after they managed to get out of their lorry before it plunged into a ravine formed by a landslide along Jalan Aring-Kenyir near the Sungai Deka Elephant Conservation Centre in Hulu Terengganu yesterday. Hulu Terengganu district police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said the couple, aged 57 and 55, were travelling from their home in Ajil to Kuala Krai, Kelantan, to collect fruit supplies when the incident occurred at about 3.40pm, according to Kosmo! Sharudin said checks showed the area had long been gazetted as closed to all vehicles following the landslide.

items.title: Rais Yatim arrives at Ayer Keroh court to face sedition charge
items.summary: MELAKA: Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Rais Yatim arrived at the Ayer Keroh Court Complex at 8.30am today to face a sedition charge linked to the Negri Sembilan royal crisis. Rais subsequently entered Sessions Court 2. Media reports yesterday, citing the e-Court system, said the 84-year-old was scheduled to be charged before Sessions Court 2 judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin.

items.title: Najib makes first public appearance since conditional pardon [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak appeared in public today for the first time since he was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest. The decision allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to stipulated conditions. For now, however, Najib remains an inmate at Kajang Prison.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia finalising measures to protect MSMEs from foreign e-commerce
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 25 — The MADANI government is finalising follow-up measures to address the concerns of local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) affected by competition from foreign e-commerce platforms, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the issue was raised directly in bilateral discussions with China’s top leadership, as well as in business meetings during his working visit to the country. Anwar said he welcomed Premier Li Qiang’s commitment to identify the best way to protect local MSMEs and prevent further impact.

items.title: HR minister: Malaysia, Nepal agree on new mechanism to curb migrant worker exploitation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Malaysia and Nepal have agreed to streamline their labour recruitment mechanism to ensure a more orderly, transparent and integrity-driven process, while curbing practices that could lead to worker exploitation. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the commitment was expressed during a phone call with his Nepali counterpart, Minister of Youth, Labour and Employment, Ramjee Yadav. The call also touched on bilateral ties in labour and employment.

items.title: Nurul Izzah pays tribute to late uncle 'Uncle Ros'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nurul Izzah Anwar has paid tribute to her late uncle, Idrus Ibrahim, fondly known as "Uncle Ros", describing him as a big-hearted man who embraced everyone with warmth and affection. In a Facebook post, the eldest daughter of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Uncle Ros was a teacher and a cherished figure in her family. "Uncle was a person of great spirit and boundless love, who always treated everyone with warmth and a sense of kinship," she said.

items.title: Najib’s family still awaiting house arrest SOP, says daughter
items.summary: Nooryana Najwa, one of Najib’s daughters, said neither the family nor his lawyers had received details from the Prisons Department, including on any modifications needed to the residence for the house arrest arrangement, according to a report by Berita Harian . So we are still waiting for information from the Prisons Department,” she said. As family members, we have not received any word or information from prison officers,” she said.

items.title: Planning a weekend trip? KTMB just added 63,000 seats to the KL-Johor ETS route
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is providing four additional ETS services for the KL Sentral-JB Sentral-KL Sentral route every weekend until Dec 27 to meet growing passenger demand for the southern sector. KTMB, in a statement yesterday, said the additional services will operate on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays over 50 days, offering 63,200 extra seats, with ticket sales opened since Sept 7. With the addition, KTMB said 12 ETS services are available for the KL Sentral-JB Sentral-KL Sentral route, including eight existing services, bringing the total weekend capacity to 189,600 seats.

items.title: Haze improves, 4 Sarawak areas record unhealthy API
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions are improving, with only four areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today. Of the 68 API monitoring stations nationwide, four recorded unhealthy readings (101-200), while 61 recorded moderate readings (51-100) and three recorded good readings (0-50). No stations recorded very unhealthy or hazardous readings.

items.title: Turkiye rejects Netanyahu's 'baseless accusations' at UN
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Turkiye rejected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's "baseless accusations" at the United Nations, its state-run news agency Anadolu reported on Friday. Netanyahu had called Turkiye's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan a "tyrant" during a fiery speech at the UN, accusing Ankara of harbouring Hamas leaders. "Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's use of the UN General Assembly podium to level 'baseless accusations' against Turkiye and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan was incompatible with the 'ideals of peace, law and dialogue' represented by the UN," Duran said.

items.title: Sarawak expected to gain 15 new parliamentary seats under proposed redelineation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Sarawak is expected to gain 15 new parliamentary seats under a proposed electoral boundary redelineation exercise, which would bring the number of parliamentary constituencies in the state from 31 to 46 and help ensure Sabah and Sarawak collectively account for one-third of representation in the Dewan Rakyat. Based on proposed electoral boundary documents shared with Berita Harian , the increase would raise Sarawak’s parliamentary seats from the current 31 to 46. The Dewan Rakyat currently has 222 seats, comprising 166 in Peninsular Malaysia and 56 in Sabah and Sarawak, with 31 in Sarawak and 25 in Sabah.

items.title: On trip to China, Anwar mourns death of elder brother Idrus at home
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — The late Idrus Ibrahim, the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, showed no unusual signs before passing away in his sleep at his home in Cheruk Tokkun, here, yesterday. His daughter, Aida Rafizah Idrus, 54, said her late father, 83, who previously suffered a heart attack last year, had recovered and only had a poor appetite lately. She said although her late father’s leg strength was no longer as strong as it used to be, he could still get up, walk, and manage himself.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against greenback, major currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the greenback and major currencies on Friday, amid mixed movements in the foreign exchange market. At 8am, the ringgit increased to 4.0810/0865 against the US dollar from Thursday's close of 4.0840/0880. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said movements in the United States (US) Treasury yields continued to influence market sentiment, with the yield on 30-year US Treasury bonds rising eight basis points to 5.48 per cent, its highest level in two decades.

items.title: Nepal floods were 'a warning to the world,' prime minister tells UN
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: The catastrophic Nepal flooding last month was "not just a local tragedy, it was a warning to the world," the country's Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the United Nations on Thursday. Shah said a warming climate was "destabilising the fragile Himalayan ecology," melting permafrost and glaciers and accelerating hazards. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: PDRM tightens security at Wisma Negeri following exco revocation
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), particularly the Negeri Sembilan police contingent, continues to prioritise public safety and order in light of current developments in the state. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the PDRM acknowledges the statement from the Attorney General’s Chambers regarding the proclamation dated April 19 and respects the ongoing constitutional and legal processes without making any determinations beyond its jurisdiction. “PDRM has implemented access management to the Wisma Negeri Office for the former line-up of Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMKN) members immediately following the announcement of the cancellation of their appointments made by the Negeri Sembilan Palace.

items.title: Najib's family yet to receive house arrest SOP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Najib Razak's family has yet to receive any information, including standard operating procedures (SOPs), from authorities on his proposed house arrest. Najib's fourth child, Nooryana Najwa, said the family and lawyers had also yet to receive any information from the Prisons Department, including details on modifications to the house to facilitate the house arrest. So, we are still waiting for information from the Prisons Department.

items.title: Rais Yatim expected to be charged in Ayer Keroh court today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Rais Yatim is expected to be charged at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court in Melaka today. A check of the e-Kehakiman portal showed Rais listed for proceedings before Judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin at 9am, while Rais has also reportedly confirmed the matter when contacted by the media, Astro Awani reported. Rais was reported to have attended a ceremony proclaiming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan at a hotel in Alor Gajah, Melaka, on June 5.

items.title: The Chias keep Teochew tradition alive, one pastry at a time [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Chia Chin Chong fights back tears as he recalls the sacrifices his father made to keep their family bakery alive. The 26-year-old had watched his father, Chia Seng Chee, labour at Ming Yi Bakery, turning out traditional Teochew pastries to support their family of four. Ming Yi began in Pulau Ketam in 1977, when Seng Chee's father, Chia Kek Leng, started making pastries while working in the family's existing catering business.

items.title: Being project-focused at work: Collaboration and purpose
items.summary: A project-focused approach requires us to look beyond individual tasks and understand the larger purpose behind the work. People may complete their individual responsibilities successfully, yet the overall result may fall short. A clear purpose provides direction.

items.title: Green shipping hits rough seas
items.summary: KLANG: The shipping industry's push towards greener fuels has hit rough waters, with scarce alternative-fuel supply, inadequate bunkering infrastructure and limited access to green financing slowing the transition. The biggest constraint is the limited global supply of green methanol, which is emerging as a key bottleneck in the maritime sector's shift to cleaner fuels. Malaysia Shipowners' Association chairman Mohamed Safwan Othman said that more ships are returning to liquified natural gas (LNG), which is not a fully zero-carbon fuel.

items.title: US Democrats criticise lavish Trump-Xi summit as lacking substance
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Senate Democrats criticised President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, saying it prioritised pageantry over substance on issues such as artificial intelligence, trade, critical minerals and weapons for Taiwan. In a statement signed by at least 19 of the 47 members of the Democratic caucus and seen by Reuters, the Democrats called on Trump to immediately deliver more than US$15 billion in security assistance — US$1.3 billion in funds and a US$14 billion arms sale package — that Congress has approved for Taiwan and to push for human rights and the release of wrongfully detained Americans. Some of Trump's fellow Republicans also marked the summit by calling on Trump to release the funds for Taiwan.

items.title: Argentine poverty rate climbs, in setback for Milei
items.summary: BUENOS AIRES, (Argentina): Argentina's poverty rate increased to 32.3 per cent in the first half of 2026, partly erasing gains made under President Javier Milei as incomes fail to keep step with rising prices, official statistics showed Thursday. The rate of extreme poverty also shot up from 6.3 per cent to 7.5 per cent. Children were the worst hit, with 44.5 per cent of Argentines aged 14 years and younger classified as poor, and 10.8 per cent as extremely poor.

items.title: Saudi reports fresh Houthi attacks as France offers military support
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles on Thursday after issuing warnings for several regions including Makkah, as France vowed to send "military means" to help shield the key Saudi oil terminal of Yanbu. Since then, the Houthis have imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, hitting its tankers and territory and seizing swathes of Yemen's Red Sea coast, which is vital for Saudi oil exports. The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's government since 2015 against the Houthis said six ballistic missiles had been intercepted, thwarting attacks on Taif and Yanbu.

items.title: Colombia's new US-backed government cuts ties with Iran
items.summary: BOGOTA: Colombia said Thursday it had cut diplomatic ties with Iran, the latest Washington ally in Latin America to sever links with the US arch-foe. Colombia's new right-wing president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has redrawn Colombia's alliances since taking over from his leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro on Aug 7 with the full-throated endorsement of US President Donald Trump. His government said Thursday the decision to cut ties with Iran, which took effect on Sept 19, was based on "hemispheric national security" considerations.

items.title: Explainer: The Mindanao peace process and the road to Kuala Lumpur
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three decades after peace talks began, the Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) are still working to complete key parts of a 2014 agreement aimed at ending decades of conflict in Mindanao. Why Kuala Lumpur? Kuala Lumpur has hosted rounds of negotiations between the Philippine government and MILF, as well as meetings on implementation of the peace agreement.

items.title: UN General Assembly walkout: Malaysia, Indonesia among nations protesting Netanyahu's address
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: Dozens of envoys from across the world walked out of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech to the UN on Thursday in protest at the Israeli leader. Delegates jeered and booed, while Netanyahu's own team stood and applauded, and the speaker of the session shouted for order. The hall, sparsely filled earlier in the session, gradually filled up before Netanyahu's speech.

items.title: KL hosts fresh Philippines-MILF peace talks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Philippine government and Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) negotiators are due to meet in Kuala Lumpur today to advance a peace process that began three decades ago. The one-day Special Meeting of the Government of the Philippines (GPH) and MILF Peace Implementation Panels will focus on outstanding commitments under the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB). The peace talks began in 1997, while the CAB, signed in 2014, provides the framework for the peace process and contains commitments that the parties are still working to implement.

items.title: Airbus identifies A321neo defect, says no safety risk
items.summary: MEXICO CITY: Airbus said on Thursday it had identified and contained a "quality issue" in the fuselage structure of its A321neo aircraft, but that planes could continue operating as it does not pose a safety risk. A source familiar with the matter said the defect affects about 500 aircraft, including roughly 250 already in service and 250 in production. The source said Airbus first spotted the problem over the summer.

items.title: Haze doesn’t just hurt your lungs: Experts warn of hidden damage to skin, scalp and eyes
items.summary: According to UM Specialist Centre consultant dermatologist Dr Nik Aimee Azizah Faheem, these tiny particles are insidious. These particles can penetrate our tissue, be it the skin, lungs, or eyes. “Particulate matter in haze can penetrate the skin, causing oxidative stress and inflammation.

items.title: Beyond reconciliation: How the National Population and Family Development Board helps non-Muslim couples part ways peacefully
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The National Population and Family Development Board’s (LPPKN) Mediator Body Pilot Project extends its support beyond marriage reconciliation, helping non-Muslim couples separate amicably while continuing to fulfil their responsibilities as parents. Dr Sarada Devi R. Subramaniam, a psychology officer and registered counsellor with LPPKN’s Family Well-being Division (Counselling and Intervention Unit), said the initiative aimed to help couples make mature decisions and understand that their parental responsibilities remained unchanged despite changes in their marital status. Sarada Devi said the collaboration with JPN enabled registered LPPKN counsellors to assist in handling marriage tribunal cases involving non-Muslim couples by giving both parties a space to share their marital concerns separately.

items.title: Rohingya caught between Malaysia crackdown and Myanmar’s uncertain welcome
items.summary: YANGON, Sept 25 — As a Rohingya exile who abandoned his life in Malaysia to return to Myanmar, Ismail’s bleak prospects may portend what awaits others caught in Kuala Lumpur’s migrant crackdown. “People without a country like us, we have nowhere to come back (to),” said Ismail, using a pseudonym for security reasons like other Rohingya in this story. “We are the most discriminated people,” said Ismail, “the people from nowhere”.

items.title: Police arrest actors, politicians protesting against Netanyahu outside UN
items.summary: NEW YORK: Police arrested at least 30 people, including actors and politicians, as they protested outside United Nations headquarters on Thursday against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of his speech at the General Assembly. Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon, Emmy winner Hannah Einbinder, Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and New York City Council member Chi Osse were among those arrested. Around 200 people gathered outside the United Nations in identical white T-shirts bearing slogans including "Fund people not bombs", "No war" and "Free Palestine".

items.title: Trump tells countries to quit ICC. Few follow his lead
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: President Donald Trump urged countries to leave the International Criminal Court immediately, calling it "evil" and a "rogue institution", but only Naoero, a tiny Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru, has followed suit during the UN General Assembly this week. Parties to the statute include 125 countries. The US has imposed financial sanctions and visa bans on court staff, and officials have prepared sanctions that could undercut the court's ability to operate, sources familiar with the matter said.

items.title: UN approves resolution on dealing with rising sea levels
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: The United Nations on Thursday passed a unanimous resolution demanding stronger action on rising sea levels, an existential threat for low-lying island nations driven by ocean warming and melting ice sheets and glaciers. In 2024, global sea levels rose by almost six millimetres, the largest annual increase ever recorded, and they are set to rise by a metre or more by the end of the century without drastic action. "Sea-level rise is measured in millimetres, but its toll is measured in millions of shattered lives, uprooted communities, and stolen futures," Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said.

items.title: US airlines oppose China's bid to add more flights
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The head of industry group Airlines for America said on Thursday that US carriers oppose adding more direct flights from China to the United States, even as Chinese President Xi Jinping raised the idea. Chris Sununu, who heads the group representing American Airlines, United Airlines, Delta Air Lines and others, said US carriers continue to be hampered by the fact that Chinese counterparts are allowed to overfly Russia on eight flights. Currently, the United States and China each can operate around 50 round-trip flights per week.

items.title: Two large pythons captured in Baling over 48 hours
items.summary: BALING: The Civil Defence Force captured two large pythons, including one that had swallowed a goat. Baling Civil Defence officer Mohd Faizol Ab Aziz said the first python, nearly 10m long and weighing 45kg, was found in front of the Ibu dan Anak rural clinic in Kampung Teluk Teduri on Tuesday. He said the team received a call about the reptile at 11.58pm.

items.title: Healthcare bodies need more funding, says association
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) has urged the government to increase funding for three critical healthcare bodies, warning that sustained underinvestment could weaken oversight and standards. Association president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said the Malaysian Medical Council (MMC), Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC) and Malaysian Society for Quality in Health (MSQH) formed the backbone of the healthcare ecosystem but faced funding pressures. The MMC regulates medical practitioners and upholds professional standards, the MHTC drives medical tourism, while the MSQH oversees hospital accreditation, quality improvement and patient safety across public and private facilities.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines expands China network, digital partnerships
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines Bhd is expanding its presence in China as passenger traffic on its China network rises 27 per cent in the first half of this year, backed by stronger travel demand between Malaysia and the country. Malaysia Aviation Group Bhd president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the country remained a priority growth market for Malaysia Airlines. In 2026, Malaysia Airlines restored daily services to Chengdu and introduced new daily flights to Shenzhen and Changsha.

items.title: North Korea vows to keep nukes 'forever'
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea will keep its nuclear weapons "forever", its foreign minister vowed yesterday, dismissing the South Korean president's renewed calls for a denuclearised Korean Peninsula. The foreign minister's remarks came a day after South Korean President Lee Jae-myung told the United Nations (UN) General Assembly he wanted to halt further growth in Pyongyang's weapons capabilities and eventually achieve a Korean Peninsula "free from nuclear weapons". The South Korean president said last week that United States President Donald Trump "clearly wants dialogue" with Pyongyang.

items.title: Xi and Trump call for peace in lavish White House state visit
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Xi Jinping called Thursday for the United States and China to manage their superpower rivalry and keep AI under human control as President Donald Trump gave his Chinese counterpart a lavish welcome at the White House Trump shook hands with Xi at the start of a day full of pomp and pageantry, but their talks will focus on tense issues – particularly how to handle the rising challenges posed by artificial intelligence. "Working together, President Xi and I have made tremendous strides on the issues facing our two countries," Trump said. 'STRONG, VIBTRANT AND FIT' Few breakthroughs are expected during Xi's state visit.

items.title: Leukaemia-stricken boy's dream of riding in police car comes true
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: A four-year-old boy battling leukaemia had his dream of riding in a police patrol car come true today, thanks to the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters. Hilmy said the family had long known of Hafiz's fascination with the police, particularly his excitement whenever he saw police vehicles. "He really loves police cars and the police.

items.title: N. Sembilan Ruler formally revokes appointments of 10 exco members
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir has revoked the appointments of 10 state executive council members, according to a state government gazette. The gazette said Tuanku Muhriz withdrew his consent and cancelled their appointments after stating that they had breached their oath of loyalty. The 10 affected Exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Haji Zaifulbahri Haji Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Haji Mohd Asna Haji Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: High Court to rule Oct 23 on bid to stop RHB closing shipping firm’s accounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The High Court here today fixed October 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit. He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care. In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.

items.title: MACC, FBI step up cooperation to tackle corruption, cross-border crime, says chief commissioner
items.summary: MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was among the matters discussed during a courtesy visit by an FBI delegation led by Law Enforcement Attaché Varinder Singh to the MACC headquarters here today. Also present were MACC senior directors Datuk Y.S. Karunanithy (Special Operations Division), Datuk Saiful Ezral Arifin (Intelligence Division), and director Datuk Saiful Hazmi Mohd Saad (Legal and Prosecution Division), as well as FBI Assistant Law Enforcement Attaché Cody Kirk.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN to negotiate with other parties soon, says Ab Rauf
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 24 — Negotiations for cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and other parties for the 16th Melaka State Election are expected to be held soon, says Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said the negotiations would begin as soon as he receives the green light from the top Umno and BN leadership. Ab Rauf said the 21 state seats won by BN in the 15th state election would form the basis of the coalition's negotiations.

items.title: Malaysia, China agree on proposed ECRL extension to Rantau Panjang, says Anwar
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia and China have agreed on the proposed extension of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, Kelantan, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said he also received positive feedback on the proposal during his discussions with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. Also present at the press conference were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, and Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.

items.title: Tengku Zafrul asks N. Sembilan MB to name who allegedly forced him to sign proclamation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has been urged to explain who allegedly forced him to sign the Instrument of Proclamation regarding the position of Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir on August 3. Senior Political Advisor to the Prime Minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz said the question remained unanswered despite Ismail issuing a seven-page statement on the issue. Tengku Zafrul asked in a Facebook post today.

items.title: Former Petronas manager met Petros official before job interview, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Sessions Court today heard that former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal Mohd Jasni met informally with a senior official of Petroleum Sarawak Berhad (Petros) at the Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC), before a formal interview for a position at the company in 2024. The fifth prosecution witness, a former Petronas employee, said the meeting took place before Mohd Khairul Akmal’s interview with Petros chief financial officer and chief executive officer, Mohd Azha Abdul Jalil and Datuk Janin Girie, respectively, at the company’s office in Kuching, Sarawak. The witness said Mohd Khairul Akmal applied for the position of Head of Upstream Finance at Petros in 2024, while he was Manager of Business Planning Performance Review Upstream at Petronas.

items.title: Anwar’s elder brother Idrus Ibrahim dies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today shared the sad news of the death of his elder brother, Idrus Ibrahim. In a Facebook post, Anwar said he received the heartbreaking news while returning to Malaysia from a three-day working visit to China. The prime minister also prayed for the deceased to be forgiven for his shortcomings, showered with mercy and placed among Allah’s faithful servants who do good deeds.

items.title: Man rams traffic policeman, injures him while fleeing Ipoh roadblock
items.summary: Ipoh District Police Chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said that during the 9.45am incident, police managed to arrest the 29-year-old man after his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction. “Three traffic personnel then pursued the car. “The driver then fled towards Gunung Lang, and upon reaching the area near McDonald’s Gunung Lang, the driver drove against the flow of traffic before his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Rapid KL to offer free shuttle buses for Bahrain GP at Sepang
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — Rapid KL, in collaboration with Sepang International Circuit (SIC), will provide free shuttle bus services in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the SIC from October 2-4. Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the special shuttle bus service to SIC would operate from three locations, namely the bus hub at Level 1 of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2, the Mitsui KLIA bus hub and De-Village, Persiaran Millenia 2, Bandar Baru Enstek. To complement the service, Rapid KL will also provide shuttle buses within the circuit to facilitate visitors’ movement to key locations.

items.title: PM Anwar: China visit yields RM28b in potential investments across high‑tech sectors
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia has secured more than RM28 billion in potential investments following trade talks with major Chinese industry players, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The high-impact investments span several strategic sectors, including semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence, robotics, electric vehicles, biotechnology, and advanced medical devices. “Overall, these business meetings recorded potential investments valued at over RM28 billion,” said Anwar.

items.title: Air quality dips in Sarawak with nine areas unhealthy, Melaka also affected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — A total of nine areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4pm today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording the highest reading at 200. Meanwhile, 48 areas recorded moderate readings, including Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (75); Keningau, Sabah (60); Seberang Perai, Penang (53); and Kota Bharu, Kelantan (52). Another 11 areas recorded good readings.

items.title: Emrail loses RM59m LRT3 bond suit, ordered to pay Kuwait Finance House RM39m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — In a double courtroom defeat for rail contractor Emrail Sdn Bhd, the High Court has dismissed its RM59.1 million lawsuit against Kuwait Finance House (M) Bhd (KFH) and ordered the company alongside three personal guarantors to pay the bank RM39.09 million. Justice Quay Chew Soon dismissed Emrail's claim over a disputed performance bond for the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) development in its entirety and allowed KFH’s counterclaim in full, holding the contractor and its guarantors jointly and severally liable for the outstanding debt, FMT reported. The court further established that the specific performance bond template required by Emrail was never incorporated into the financing agreement with KFH.

items.title: MCMC backs police crackdown as Op Pedo nets 53 suspects, eight of them teens
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The collaboration between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) continues to be strengthened to combat the misuse of network services for the purpose of online child sexual exploitation. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, as the technical agency, would continue to play an important role in assisting PDRM, especially the D11 Division (Sexual, Women and Child Investigation) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), in tracking down those who misuse network services and subsequently bringing them to justice. Fahmi said the collaboration also involved technical and forensic aspects to assist PDRM investigations into online child sexual exploitation activities.

items.title: Sabah sees 10 million searches on Xiaohongshu as China tourism interest surges
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah has recorded over 10 million searches on REDnote (Xiaohongshu), China’s leading social and lifestyle platform, signalling a massive surge in interest from Chinese travellers, said Datuk Jafry Ariffin The Sabah minister of tourism, culture and environment disclosed the figures following his visit to the REDnote office in Shanghai yesterday, noting that the high search volume underscores Sabah’s strong visibility in the Chinese market. “This is a very encouraging indication for Sabah. “China remains an important tourism market for Sabah.

items.title: Masidi confident Putrajaya will secure Sabah borders amid Balabac Strait concerns
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun is confident the federal government will safeguard the state's borders in the Balabac Strait, despite concerns surrounding a US-backed Philippine military facility in the region. Speaking to reporters after the Sabah Carbon Forum today, Masidi said that border security falls under the jurisdiction of Putrajaya. When asked if Sabah would see additional security reinforcements, Masidi replied, “All I can say is that I don’t think they will allow Sabah to go undefended.”
